name: Shipping chokepoints
summary: Iran says two tankers hit mines near Hormuz on 15 Nov and a supertanker sank; claim unconfirmed; strait restricted
state: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on 15 Nov that two tankers on an unauthorised route in the southern Strait of Hormuz hit naval mines and that a supertanker carrying more than two million barrels sank; no independent confirmation was reported (Middle East Eye; Anadolu Agency). Iran's regular navy said a third tanker was hit east of the strait (India TV). Iran has restricted the strait since July and the US enforces a blockade of Iranian ports, so Hormuz traffic remains materially impeded.
for_you: Check FCDO travel advice and UKMTO notices for the Gulf. Disruption at Hormuz tends to raise fuel, freight and delivery costs worldwide.

sources.title: Middle East Eye — Two oil tankers ablaze after striking naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz
India TV — Three oil tankers catch fire in Strait of Hormuz, Iran blames naval mines

why: Around 30% of seaborne oil and much container trade passes Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Suez, Panama and Malacca; disruption raises prices worldwide.
drivers: Houthi/Iran attacks, war-risk insurance, drought (Panama), naval incidents, piracy.

rubric.alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, or any chokepoint closed, or two or more disrupted at once.
rubric.watch: One chokepoint disrupted (attacks, large-scale diversions, draught restrictions).
